name: Role of financial management
subpoints: strategic role of financial management — managing the funds of the business so it meets its goals — a long-term view, not just paying the bills
objectives — profitability — the ability to maximise profit; measured by gross profit, net profit and return on equity
objectives — growth — the ability to increase in size in the long term
objectives — efficiency — minimising costs and managing assets so maximum profit comes from the lowest possible level of assets
objectives — liquidity — the ability to pay short-term liabilities as they fall due
objectives — solvency — the ability to pay both short-term and long-term liabilities as they fall due
short-term and long-term objectives — and the conflicts between them — growth now usually costs profit now
interdependence with other key business functions — finance with operations, marketing and human resources

shots.note: Straight at the objectives dot point. Define liquidity, then say why a business needs it.
The short-term versus long-term conflict, set on a sole trader whose sales are growing so fast she needs $10 000 of stock. Growth versus liquidity.
Part (d) is the interdependence question — finance and operations, with examples. Part (c) covers solvency.
“Debts paid as they fall due” is doing the work here — read it carefully, because it decides between liquidity and solvency.
Which objective the expense ratio measures. Markers repeatedly penalise students for calling this a profitability ratio — it is efficiency.
Profitability and efficiency pulling in opposite directions across two businesses. Work out both ratios before you choose.

textOnly.text: Explain a possible conflict between ONE short-term and ONE long-term financial objective.
textOnly.note: The same idea as the screenshot above, asked with no stimulus at all.

textOnly.text: Outline how the short-term and long-term financial goals of this business may conflict.
textOnly.note: Food Plus Pty Ltd, a health food grocer opening three stores in the USA.

textOnly.text: Why is efficiency a financial objective?
textOnly.note: Marker’s note: the definition must cover minimising costs AND managing assets — maximum profit from the lowest possible level of assets.

textOnly.text: Explain the interdependence between marketing and finance for this business.
textOnly.note: A business selling stylish, high-performance luxury cars.

textOnly.text: Using the data, analyse the interdependence between human resources management and financial management in this business.
textOnly.note: Comes with two years of HR data — training spend, absenteeism, accidents, strike days, staff turnover — and total HR costs.

textOnly.header: Barker Trial 2023, Question 25 — part of a 20-mark report
textOnly.text: Examine the interdependence between finance and human resources for this business.
textOnly.note: Marvel Metals, where rising wages are squeezing profitability and new technology means retraining and redundancies.

textOnly.text: A business closely monitors their financial records to minimise their expenses and manage assets so that maximum profit is achieved with the lowest possible level of assets. What financial objective does this best illustrate?
textOnly.note: Answer: efficiency. Note how the stem is just the definition, rearranged.

textOnly.header: St Ignatius’ Trial 2023, Question 2 — multiple choice
textOnly.text: Liquidity is defined as the extent to which a business can… (fund shareholder dividends / pay long term debts as they fall due / collect its accounts receivable on time / meet its financial commitments in the short term)
textOnly.note: Answer: D. Option B is solvency — the classic distractor.

textOnly.header: St Ignatius’ Trial 2024, Question 1 — multiple choice
textOnly.text: Budgeting for the acquisition of staff needs is an example of interdependence between which of the following business functions?
textOnly.note: Answer: finance and human resources.

textOnly.text: The training of staff in the manufacturing process is an example of interdependence between which of the following business functions?
textOnly.note: Answer: operations and human resources.

name: Influences on financial management
subpoints: internal sources of finance — retained profits — the cheapest and most flexible source
external sources — debt, short-term — overdraft, commercial bills, factoring
external sources — debt, long-term — mortgage, debentures, unsecured notes, leasing
external sources — equity — ordinary shares (new issues, rights issues, placements, share purchase plans) and private equity — see Topic 6
financial institutions — banks, investment banks, finance companies, superannuation funds, life insurance companies, unit trusts, the Australian Securities Exchange
influence of government — the Australian Securities and Investments Commission, and company taxation
global market influences — economic outlook, availability of funds, interest rates

shots.note: The financial institutions dot point, tested directly. You have to know which institution actually provides leasing.
ASIC — the government influence. Note how the stem describes what it does rather than naming it.
The main written question on government influence. Cover both ASIC and company taxation.
Global market influences — a downturn in the economic outlook working through unemployment, output and exchange rates.
Internal versus external sources, compared, for a specific purchase. The biggest sources-of-finance question in the collection.

textOnly.text: Which of the following financial institutions take funds from a large number of small investors and invests them in specific types of financial assets?
textOnly.note: Answer: unit trusts.

textOnly.header: St Ignatius’ Trial 2024, Question 12 — multiple choice
textOnly.text: Which of the following is correct for a unit trust? (Investors buy direct from ASX / Investor funds are pooled and distributed upon retirement / They are only for investment by sophisticated investors / Investor funds are pooled, and assets purchased on their behalf)
textOnly.note: Answer: D. Option B describes a superannuation fund.

textOnly.text: Describe how the Australian Securities and Investment Commission impacts this business.
textOnly.note: Set on the Bakers Dozen balance sheet. The school’s marking guide prints a different version of this question asking about company taxation instead — worth practising both.

textOnly.text: Explain TWO global influences on the financial management of this business.
textOnly.note: Answers: global economic outlook, availability of funds, interest rates, exchange rates.

textOnly.text: Discuss TWO sources of finance that Food Plus Pty Ltd can use to fund its expansion.
Compare and contrast TWO sources of debt finance used by Local Grocer Pty Ltd.
textOnly.note: Compare and contrast means similarities AND differences — e.g. overdraft against mortgage.

textOnly.text: Explain a financial risk associated with borrowing funds from the USA.
textOnly.note: A luxury Australian handbag business borrowing US$30 million. Availability of funds and exchange rate risk together.

textOnly.text: Analyse how different sources of finance impact the financial objectives of a business.
textOnly.note: The marking guide wants explicit links from each source to profitability, growth, efficiency, liquidity and solvency.

textOnly.text: Analyse the influence of government and the global market on financial management strategies.

name: Planning and implementing
subpoints: financial needs — how much the business needs and what for
budgets — operating, project and financial budgets
record systems — the mechanisms for keeping accurate financial records
financial risks — the danger that debts cannot be repaid
financial controls — policies to prevent loss, waste and fraud — clear authorisation, separation of duties, rotation of duties, control of cash
debt and equity financing — the advantages and disadvantages of each
matching the terms and source of finance to business purpose — short-term finance for short-term needs, long-term finance for long-term assets

shots.note: The whole process in one question, and the sequence you have to know: determining financial needs, developing budgets, maintaining record systems, identifying financial risks, establishing financial controls.
Matching the source of finance to the purpose — a property is a long-term asset, so it needs long-term finance.
Matching again, but for a short-term need. Stock before a busy trading period calls for short-term sources.
The best written question on matching terms and source of finance to purpose.
Part (b) is the debt half of the debt-versus-equity dot point — pair it with 22(c) in Topic 6 for the full comparison. Part (a) is the ethical-issues question, so this crop appears again in Topic 4.
Comparative ratio analysis as a decision tool — note that raw totals mislead when the two businesses are different sizes.
The same idea, asked from the investor’s side.

name: Ethical issues of financial statements
subpoints: audited accounts — internal, management or independent external audits
record keeping — accurate and honest recording of all transactions
reporting practices — statements that reflect the true position and performance of the business
inappropriate cut-off periods — shifting revenue or expenses between periods to flatter a result
misuse of funds — employees or managers taking money or stock
— examined alongside — — limitations of financial reports: normalised earnings, capitalising expenses, valuing assets, timing issues, debt repayments, notes to the financial statements

shots.note: The only written ethical-issues question in the 2012–2020 HSC papers. Part (a) is the one you want here.
Capitalising expenses — legal fees buried in the asset value of a warehouse. The classic limitations question.

textOnly.text: Explain ONE ethical issue related to financial reports for the stakeholders of this business.
textOnly.note: Set on the Playsmart Child Care balance sheet, which carries $100 000 of goodwill and a $320 000 building. The marking guide wants transparency about how those were valued, and the risk that a lender is misled.

textOnly.text: Outline ONE ethical issue related to this financial report.
textOnly.note: Marking guide accepts: audited accounts, record keeping, reporting practices, inappropriate cut-off periods, misuse of funds.

textOnly.text: Describe TWO limitations of SK Pty Ltd’s 2024 Balance Sheet.
textOnly.note: Answer runs on valuing assets (equipment depreciates, and depreciation is an estimate) and capitalising expenses ($60 000 of R&D recorded as a non-current asset).

textOnly.text: Explain ONE limitation of financial statements in providing a complete picture of Coffee Mania’s financial health.
Outline ONE limitation of financial reports.

name: Profitability and working capital management
subpoints: working capital — control of current assets — cash, receivables, inventories
working capital — control of current liabilities — payables, loans, overdrafts
working capital — strategies — leasing, sale and lease back
profitability — cost controls — fixed and variable costs, cost centres, expense minimisation
profitability — revenue controls — marketing objectives (sales mix, pricing policy)
— measured by — — profitability ratios: gross profit ratio, net profit ratio, return on equity ratio · liquidity: current ratio

shots.note: Straight to the point — which action immediately improves working capital.
The benchmark working capital business report: “recommend TWO appropriate working capital management strategies for this business”.
Lee’s Catering. The best single question in the collection — working capital AND profitability in one report, and every figure in the stimulus is there to be used.
Kingland Office Supplies. Low profitability, an unappealing product mix, poor cash flow and poor accounts receivable turnover — revenue controls and receivables together.

Sportyz Goodz. Sales and profit both falling, with profit falling faster — read the graph and the widening gap points straight at costs. Its first bullet also covers the strategic role of financial management from Topic 1.
Accounts receivable turnover and the expense ratio, off one stimulus.
Part (c) is the key receivables-control question: recommend a strategy to improve efficiency in collecting accounts receivable.
How to improve management of accounts receivable turnover.
Factoring. Remember it cuts both ways — better cash flow, worse profitability.
Chalker Pty Ltd — calculate the current ratio from a full balance sheet.
Same balance sheet, gearing this time.
Steve’s Lawn Services. Note that stock is left blank — that is the whole trick of Question 12 below.
Question 11 is equity for a sole trader; Question 12 cannot be answered at all, because stock is missing from the stimulus.
Kerry’s Warehouse — liquidity and gearing against both the industry average and last year.
Gross profit ratio, net profit ratio and expense ratio off one table.
The 2020 version of the liquidity-and-gearing pair.
Gross profit ratio, and the average number of days to collect debts.
Working backwards from the ratios to sales and net profit.
The relationship between the expense ratio, gross profit ratio and net profit ratio.
Current ratio and accounts receivable turnover moving together.
Gearing ratio from a full balance sheet.
Cash flow — the opening balance carried across months.
The same skill in short-answer form.

name: Equity financing
subpoints: internal equity — the owner’s own funds put into the business, and retained profits
ordinary shares — new issues — shares offered to the public for the first time
ordinary shares — rights issues — existing shareholders offered more shares, usually at a discount
ordinary shares — placements — shares sold directly to selected institutional investors
ordinary shares — share purchase plans — existing shareholders buy a set parcel without brokerage
private equity — money invested in a private company not listed on the ASX
advantages and disadvantages — no repayment and no interest, so lower risk · but ownership is diluted, returns must be shared, and it is slower and more expensive to raise

shots.note: Rights issues — the discount to existing shareholders is the giveaway.
A sole trader putting her own money in is internal equity finance — not a loan, and not retained profits.
The disadvantage-of-equity question. Pair it with 22(b) in Topic 3 for the full debt-versus-equity comparison.
Emu Uniform Manufacturers — recommend a source of finance for a $5 million factory expansion.

textOnly.text: Compare the use of debt and equity as sources of finance, and recommend ONE source of finance this business could use to fund its expansion.
textOnly.note: Future Century Gaming Pty Ltd, an online gaming platform funding global expansion through external sources.

textOnly.text: Compare the use of a mortgage to a new issue of shares to fund the factory purchase.
textOnly.note: Ozzi Baby Food Pty Ltd — a direct debt-versus-equity comparison, with the equity option being an ASX listing.

textOnly.text: A business is offering existing shareholders the opportunity to purchase more shares at a discount. This is known as what type of equity finance?
textOnly.note: Answer: share purchase plans.

textOnly.text: Which of the following is an external source of equity? (Overdraft / Ordinary shares / Retained profits / Debentures)
textOnly.note: Answer: ordinary shares. Retained profits are internal equity; the other two are debt.

textOnly.header: St Ignatius’ Trial 2024, Question 25 — part of a 20-mark report
textOnly.text: Discuss a suitable source of finance for this business expansion.
textOnly.note: An investor has offered the full capital in return for 51% equity — so the trade-off is losing control against borrowing at 8% interest.

name: Global financial management strategies
subpoints: exchange rates — appreciation and depreciation, and their effect on importers and exporters
interest rates — the cost of borrowing overseas versus at home
methods of international payment — payment in advance, letter of credit, clean payment, bill of exchange — ranked by risk to each side
hedging — taking action to protect against an adverse currency movement
derivatives — forward exchange contracts, options contracts, swap contracts

shots.note: Methods of international payment — an Australian business selling to French wholesalers who will not pay in advance.
Justify the method of payment that most reduces financial risk. The biggest written global question in the collection.
Hedging and derivatives — how to protect against a change in the value of the Australian dollar.
Exchange rates — how an appreciation affects an importer’s competitive position.
Who suffers most when the Australian dollar rises. Work through each option as either an importer or an exporter.
The same idea, tested on exports to Canada.

textOnly.header: Knox Grammar Trial 2023, Question 14 — multiple choice
textOnly.text: Hardwood Timber Pty Ltd has 90 days to pay an overseas supplier in US dollars. They will lock in the payment amount at today’s exchange rate. Which global financial management strategy best describes this process?
textOnly.note: Answer: a forward exchange contract. Hedging is the broader category; the forward contract is the specific instrument.

textOnly.text: Which of the following is an agreement to exchange currency in the spot market with an agreement to reverse the transaction in the future?
textOnly.note: Answer: a swap contract.

textOnly.text: An Australian candle shop imports products from overseas and sells them locally. Which method of international payment would be the highest risk for the candle shop?
textOnly.note: Answer: payment in advance — the importer pays before the goods arrive.

textOnly.text: An export company based in Sydney sells Australian-made art to the Asian market. Which form of payment has the lowest level of risk for the exporter?
textOnly.note: Answer: payment in advance. Same instrument as above — the risk just sits with the other party.

textOnly.header: Knox Grammar Trial 2023, Question 20 — multiple choice
textOnly.text: An Australian logistics company purchases their fuel from overseas suppliers. What impact would a decrease in the Australian dollar relative to all other foreign currencies have on this business?
textOnly.note: Answer: decreased net profit and increased expenses.
